reference.source: Kaplan & Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry; DSM-5-TR
clinicalPearls: Characterised by obsessions (intrusive, unwanted, distressing thoughts, images, or urges) and/or compulsions (repetitive behaviours or mental acts performed to reduce anxiety or prevent a feared outcome)
Symptoms are time-consuming or cause marked distress and functional impairment; patients often recognise them as excessive, though insight varies
Common themes include contamination with washing, doubt with checking, symmetry with ordering, and taboo intrusive thoughts
First-line treatment is cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure and response prevention, which is highly effective
Pharmacotherapy principles favour SSRIs, often needing higher doses and longer trials than in depression before judging response
Clomipramine is an effective alternative, and augmentation strategies are considered in resistant cases
Distinguish from obsessive-compulsive personality disorder, which involves ego-syntonic perfectionism and rigidity rather than distressing intrusive symptoms
Assess for comorbid depression, tic disorders, and hoarding, and ask about suicidal ideation
reference.pathophysiology: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is associated with dysfunction of cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuits, particularly hyperactivity involving the orbitofrontal cortex, anterior cingulate, and basal ganglia, together with serotonergic and glutamatergic dysregulation. Genetic factors contribute, and in some children symptom onset has been linked to post-streptococcal autoimmune processes.
additionalDifferentials: Psychotic disorder when insight is absent
additionalInvestigations: Standardised OCD severity rating scales to quantify symptoms and monitor treatment
Screening for comorbid depression, anxiety, and tic disorders
Assessment of insight and degree of functional impairment
Consideration of post-streptococcal aetiology in abrupt paediatric onset
redFlags: Suicidal ideation, particularly with comorbid depression
Severe functional incapacity from time-consuming rituals
Complete loss of insight suggesting a psychotic process
Self-harm from compulsions such as excessive washing causing skin breakdown
reference.prognosis: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is typically chronic with waxing and waning severity, but many patients achieve substantial improvement with exposure and response prevention and adequate pharmacotherapy. Early onset, poor insight, and comorbidity are associated with a more persistent course.
pitfalls: Confusing OCD with obsessive-compulsive personality disorder
Judging SSRI non-response before an adequately high dose and prolonged trial
Providing reassurance that inadvertently reinforces compulsive checking
Overlooking comorbid depression and suicide risk
Failing to offer or refer for exposure and response prevention, the most effective psychotherapy
